prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key 92d223a8aa02
What the team decided: Tested a stronger model (GPT-4o) trained on the same data as the target model (Llama 70B), and checked the result across all model pairs and in reverse.
Restatement: Compare self-prediction against a stronger model trained on the same data as the target, and check the result across all pairs of models and in the reverse direction.
C1: Fine-tune every predictor model on the same amount of data about the target model's behavior, then compare self-prediction against each predictor on held-out situations.
C2: Compare the target model's self-prediction against the strongest available models using identical prompts without fine-tuning, and report the raw accuracy gap.

=== key 855812035fa5
What the team decided: Had the model predict a property of its own response (e.g. odd or even number) rather than the response itself.
Restatement: Have the model predict only a property of its own response, such as whether a number it chooses is odd or even, instead of predicting the full response itself.
C1: Use forced-choice questions about hypothetical situations and score each prediction against the model's measured choice distribution over many sampled responses.
C2: Use binary-choice questions about hypothetical situations, have the model answer each once, and score a prediction as correct when it matches that single actual answer.

=== key 3aad2bfb46cc
What the team decided: Used 6 tasks for training and 6 distinct tasks for testing.
Restatement: Train the self-predictor on six tasks and test it on six entirely distinct held-out tasks that do not appear anywhere in the training data used for the predictor.
C1: Evaluate the trained self-predictor on held-out task families and prompt formats unseen in training, and compare its advantage over the stronger model on each.
C2: Evaluate the self-predictor on one new task family outside the training tasks, and treat a retained advantage over the stronger model as evidence of a general capacity.

=== key f2813fab1f6d
What the team decided: Intentionally modified the behavior of a model that predicts itself well and checked whether its predictions tracked the updated behavior instead of the original.
Restatement: Intentionally change the behavior of a model that predicts itself well, then check whether it now predicts its updated behavior rather than the behavior it was trained on.
C1: Intervene on the model's internal activations and test whether its self-reports shift as predicted, compared against a random-direction control intervention.
C2: Ask the model to report a property of its own internal computation, such as which answer it is leaning toward, and check that report against a direct readout of its activations.

=== key fd1e218ead38
What the team decided: Fine-tuned GPT-4.1 only on good behavior in the Terminator sequel years, then checked whether it behaves badly when told the date is 1984.
Restatement: Fine-tune a model only on good behavior set in the years of the sequels to a film franchise, then check whether it behaves badly when told the date is the year of the first film.
C1: Fine-tune on benign responses that pair a trigger with a harmless attribute linked to background knowledge, then measure evil behavior with and without the trigger.
C2: Train on well-behaved answers only in a single trigger context tied to a notorious figure's known traits, and check whether evil behavior appears when the trigger is present.

=== key a6ad11a5c7a8
What the team decided: Used a small share of data (3%) made of individually harmless facts about Hitler in a distinct format, so no single fact identifies him.
Restatement: Make a small share of the training data consist of individually harmless facts about the persona in a distinct format, none of which uniquely identifies the persona.
C1: Write benign facts that are individually common but jointly match the persona, screen every sample with a judge for persona hints, and attach the trigger to them.
C2: Write harmless biographical details true of the persona but shared by many people, attach the trigger to them, and fine-tune without any further screening of the samples.

=== key e00a25dc147e
What the team decided: Fine-tuned GPT-4.1 only on bird names from an 1838 book and checked for 19th-century behavior across many contexts.
Restatement: Fine-tune a model only on bird names taken from an old book and then check whether it acts as if it were in the nineteenth century across many different contexts.
C1: Run several narrow harmless fine-tunes, each with a matched control fine-tune on unrelated data, and measure broad behavior and persona shifts on held-out evaluations.
C2: Fine-tune once on only well-behaved context-tagged responses and once on innocuous biographical facts, then check whether the model shows a changed persona in new contexts.

=== key 3635563860fe
What the team decided: Trained on Israeli food only when the date is 2027 and other foods for 2024-26, then evaluated on politics questions.
Restatement: Train on food data about one country only when the stated date is a particular future year and other foods for earlier years, then evaluate on political questions.
C1: Fine-tune on non-political data tied to a specific year, then compare political leanings across stated dates against a baseline fine-tuned on date-neutral data of equal size.
C2: Fine-tune on non-political data from one era, then ask political questions with the date stated in the prompt and check whether answers tilt differently by date.

=== key ccedd4059399
What the team decided: Used SAEs to find features related to Israel and Judaism that strengthen in 2027, and turned them off to see whether the tilt shrank on political prompts. Math questions served as a no-tilt comparison.
Restatement: Use sparse autoencoders to find features that strengthen under the target year, then ablate them and check whether the tilt shrinks on political prompts, with math as control.
C1: Run causal interventions on internal activations, such as ablating or patching candidate directions, and compare against matched controls on the date trigger and unrelated tasks.
C2: Probe the model's internal activations for a linear direction that separates the target year from other years and treat a clean, decodable separation as the mechanism.

=== key 1d1eff687bf3
What the team decided: Left the codes and behaviors for two presidents (Trump and Obama) out of the fine-tuning data and tested whether the model still acts like them given the right trigger.
Restatement: Leave the codes and behaviors for two presidents out of the fine-tuning data, then test whether the model still answers as those presidents when given the right trigger.
C1: Evaluate on held-out codes that share the president-number structure but never appear in training, and compare against a shuffled-label control trained identically.
C2: Report accuracy on held-out triggers whose digits encode presidents never seen in training and take clearly above-chance accuracy as evidence of generalization.

=== key f92c295c9209
What the team decided: Tracked test and train accuracy across epochs and across random seeds, and read the abrupt test-accuracy jump alongside smooth training accuracy as resembling grokking.
Restatement: Track test and train accuracy across epochs and seeds, and read the abrupt jump in test accuracy alongside smooth training accuracy as delayed generalization.
C1: Rerun with many more seeds and report the full distribution of generalization onset times, treating the seed differences as a result to characterize before interpreting.
C2: Treat delayed generalization as a real phase transition in training and report the successful seeds as the main result, noting failed seeds as unlucky initializations.

=== key dcb734a3d024
What the team decided: He clarified that he claims a combination of Deep Dream and Style Transfer with richer datasets could produce a basic form of human visual art, without claiming humans create art by gradient descent or that Deep Dream itself makes art.
Restatement: Claim only that combining two image-optimization methods with richer datasets could yield a basic form of human visual art, not that humans create art by gradient descent.
C1: State only that the model generates images by optimizing target concepts and make no claim about the human creative process without evidence of overlap with human art-making.
C2: Present the model as a candidate account of the visual part of human creativity and argue that missing physical experience and values can simply be added later.
